import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’m checking a key design tension: restricting `]n` to siblings gives it a clear scope, while `]N` needs a broader set of parent groups to be useful. I’ll compare that with existing walk behavior before recommending how the two keys should relate.


The cabinets epic has finished its core implementation and is now in acceptance and go-live work. That makes parallel development feasible, but the shared card layout is an overlap point. The existing navigation API already resolves destinations for the keys and status-bar footer, so the new walks can extend that path. I also confirmed the ordering issue: temporal and record cards currently append their Properties foot after the walk rail. A shared bottom navigation slot would make the requested ordering reliable.


I recommend two clear scopes: `]n` cycles through same-type siblings, and `]N` jumps to the first note under the next occupied parent for that type. The report will call out that scope expansion explicitly. I also found that authored navigation links currently override derived destinations; preserving that behavior needs an explicit exception to the same-parent rule.


A nested-project example exposed a problem with vault-wide parent groups: `]N` could jump from a subproject straight to its own parent project. I’m narrowing the recommendation to neighboring parent notes under the same grandparent. That keeps repeated group jumps within one branch; when no neighboring parent has matching children, `]N` can explain why it has nowhere to go.


The existing navigation, group resolver, and group-row tests all pass: 67 tests across three suites. I’m now writing the report with the recommended grouping rule, a concrete card layout, the compatibility exceptions, and the specific work that can proceed alongside `bob-cli-qq`.
